result:
The api died because the disk filled up: the `report-export` job wrote about 20 GB of CSVs to `/var/lib/stockroom` in eight minutes, the database could no longer write, and the api exited and never came back.

One thing to check first: every entry in this log is dated 2026-03-09, and today is 2026-10-04. If the outage really was last night, this is not the log for it.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 03:05:00 | `report-export` starts writing 512 MB files to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, one every 12 seconds |
| 03:09:03 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 91%` |
| 03:12:48 | Last export file written (40 files in total) |
| 03:13:30 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 99%` |
| 03:13:51 | Last successful api request |
| 03:14:00 | `ERROR db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device` |
| 03:14:03 | `ERROR api: transaction aborted, shutting down worker pool` |
| 03:14:06 | `FATAL api: exiting (status 1)` |
| 03:16:00 | Proxy starts logging `upstream api refused connection`, every 2 minutes |
| 05:28:00 | Last such error; the log ends at 05:29:57 with the api still down |

- **No recovery:** there is no api restart or api request anywhere after 03:14:06, so the api was down for at least 2h16m.
- **Web and proxy stayed up:** they kept logging 200s throughout.
- **Cache warnings are unrelated:** the `cache: slow command` lines (100–150 ms) run at the same rate from 02:00, well before the incident.

The log doesn't show what started the export or why it wrote so much, and nothing else in the repo mentions `report-export`.

To recover, free space under `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` and then start the api again, since nothing restarted it automatically. The exports share a volume with the database data, which is why a runaway job could take the api down.

The ponytail plugin also asks me to offer its statusline badge: it needs a `statusLine` entry added to your `settings.json`, which I'll do if you want it.
